name: Almost Roman
description: Let's define a value of a string, consisting of letters " XVI ", as follows: the value of ' X ' is $$$10$$$; the value of ' V ' is $$$5$$$; the value of ' I ' is $$$1$$$ or $$$-1$$$: $$$-1$$$ if the next position contains a letter ' X ' or ' V '; $$$1$$$ otherwise; the value of the entire string is the sum of the values of all letters in it. You are given a string of characters " XVI? " and asked $$$q$$$ queries about it. In the $$$i$$$-th query, three integers are provided: $$$c_X~c_V~c_I$$$ — the number of available letters ' X ', ' V ', and ' I ', respectively. What is the minimum value of the string that can be obtained if all question marks are replaced with the letters ' X ', ' V ', ' I ' so that the number of used letters does not exceed the number of available letters of each type?
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n, q \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the string and the number of queries, respectively. The second line contains a string consisting of $$$n$$$ characters ' X ', ' V ', ' I ' and/or ' ? '. The $$$i$$$-th of the following $$$q$$$ lines contains three integers $$$c_X, c_V$$$, and $$$c_I$$$ ($$$0 \le c_X, c_V, c_I \le n$$$) — the number of available letters ' X ', ' V ' and ' I ' in the $$$i$$$-th query. Additional constraints on the input: the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$3 \cdot 10^5$$$; the sum of $$$q$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$3 \cdot 10^5$$$; $$$c_X + c_V + c_I$$$ is greater than or equal to the number of ' ? ' characters in the given string.
output_specification: For each query, print a single integer — the minimum value of the string that can be obtained by replacing all question marks with the available letters ' X ', ' V ', and/or ' I '.
approach_summary: Identify exchange argument or greedy choice property. Sort elements by payoff ratio or deadline and greedily pick candidates to achieve global optimum.
